claims_checked.claim: Template CITATION.cff would be inherited by every new app (real risk?)
claims_checked.evidence: The template's root files are copied when someone uses the GitHub template. The initialiser (LabConstrictor_streamlit/app.py:660-690) moves only README.md to .tools/docs/README.md and writes a new README; it never touches other root files, and replace_in_file (app.py:484) only rewrites listed placeholders. The sync workflow (.github/workflows/sync_template.yml) only runs .template_sync/migrations/*.py. The only root-file migration in the manifest list is v0_1_11_to_v0_1_12, which touches README and .tools/docs. So synchronisation neither adds nor removes a CITATION.cff, and existing apps (none has one) are unaffected. Every repo created from the template after the file is added would show GitHub 'Cite this repository' with the LabConstrictor authors and paper. A root .zenodo.json would be worse: Zenodo uses it as the only metadata source for a release (see the precedence claim) and would archive an app under LabConstrictor's creators.

gaps.requirement: Template LabConstrictor: a CITATION.cff for the framework without every new app inheriting it
gaps.current: No CITATION.cff or .zenodo.json in LabConstrictor. The initialiser moves only README.md and replaces placeholders (LabConstrictor_streamlit/app.py:484, 660-690). Sync migrations never manage root files. A file added to the template root would reach every repo created from it afterwards, and GitHub would offer 'Cite this repository' with the LabConstrictor authors and the preprint for apps that have nothing to do with the paper. Existing apps are not affected, because sync would never deliver the file.
gaps.proposal:
Real risk, avoidable in 3 steps. (1) In LabConstrictor, add root CITATION.cff with the draft below ONLY after step 2 ships. (2) In LabConstrictor_streamlit/app.py, next to the README handling (lines ~660-690), delete or overwrite the template's root CITATION.cff when the repo is initialised. The same test the README uses ('# LabConstrictor' in the file) works here: refuse to leave a CFF whose title is 'LabConstrictor' in an app. Better: generate a per-app CITATION.cff from the manifest (name, authors, license, doi becomes preferred-citation) in manifest_form.py, so each app starts with a valid file that is not the template's. (3) Never add a root .zenodo.json to the template: Zenodo would take it as the only metadata and archive any app under LabConstrictor's creators. Keep the template's Zenodo metadata in the manual record (10.5281/zenodo.19074199) and in the CFF. Until (2) ships, do nothing to the template root.

NucleiSky's pyproject.toml says 0.0.1 while its GitHub releases run to 0.1.1. Zenodo affiliations differ from the preprint's header. gaps.proposal: Do not put 'version' or 'date-released' into the CFF files until each repo has a release process that sets them (NucleiSky: bump pyproject to match the release; template: tag a release that matches what Zenodo archived). On the site, show the app's release version next to the citation, from the fetched release, as the audit asks. The version in the CFF would otherwise be a second place to forget; the site already reads the release.
